Too few ligands results in weak binding & too many may lead to steric hinderance. 3) non-specific binding sites & can be blocked or passivated. This prevents non-specific interactions. 4) Multiple binding sites on the ligands or multivalent ligands can improve specificity by increasing overall binding. 5) Employing signal amplification strategies such as Enzyme linked assays or nanomaterial based amplification enhances sensitivity. 6) Tailor the surface properties of AuNPs by functionalizing them with polymers or other molecules. 7) The size & shape of AuNPs can influence their binding properties. Fine Tuning these parameters enhance specificity for certain target molecules.

To calculate limit of Detection: 1) Measure the signal from blank sample with no target analyte 2) calculate standard deviation (SD) 3) Multiply SD by a factor and add to mean blank signal 4) The result is the LOD. LOD = 3.3 (Sy)/S, where Sy is SD of response and S is slope of calibration curve.
